preamble: Devoicing of the voiced alveolo-palatal affricate [d͡ʑ] to [t͡ɕ]. The clear case is Polish final obstruent devoicing, which neutralizes dź/dzi [d͡ʑ] with ć [t͡ɕ] word-finally, so that the stem consonant alternates between voiced [d͡ʑ] before a vowel and voiceless [t͡ɕ] at the end of the word (łodzi [ˈwɔ.d͡ʑi] ~ łódź [wut͡ɕ]). Elsewhere it is sporadic: a corpus of heritage Bosnian/Croatian/Montenegrin/Serbian in German-speaking Switzerland records a single unvoiced token of đ. Because [d͡ʑ] is itself an uncommon phoneme, the change is rare cross-linguistically.

examples.note: Word-final devoicing; łódź is homophonous in its final consonant with words spelled -ć.
The final dź is devoiced to [t͡ɕ] while the medial one stays voiced.
The imperative is homophonous with choć 'although'.

A single token from one second-generation speaker in Switzerland (transcript SB_01_B); the authors link deviant affricate realizations to the absence of /d͡ʑ/ in Swiss German. Not a systematic change.

sources: Lemmenmeier-Batinić, D., Batinić, J., & Escher, A. (2023). Map Task Corpus of Heritage BCMS spoken by second-generation speakers in Switzerland. Language Resources and Evaluation, 57. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10579-023-09634-7
